Taking on extra projects to stay distracted
e: Healthy stress management includes planning and prioritizing, breaking big tasks into smaller steps and taking short breaks to recharge. Skipping sleep increases mistakes and stress, bottling up frustration builds tension, and piling on projects adds overload.

q: An employee promises a client a report by Friday but realizes on Wednesday it will be late. The best way to manage this commitment is to
o: tell the client now and give a realistic new date
turn in an unfinished report on Friday
say nothing and deliver it Monday
ask a coworker to make an excuse
e: Managing commitments means meeting deadlines or, if you can't, telling people as early as possible and offering a realistic new date. Warning the client on Wednesday lets them plan and preserves trust. Missing the deadline silently or making excuses damages the relationship.

q: Which behavior best shows treating others with dignity and respect?
o: Listening to a coworker's idea fully before responding
Correcting a coworker's mistake in front of a client
Using a nickname a coworker has asked you not to use
e: Treating others with dignity and respect includes listening fully before responding, valuing their input and handling problems privately. Correcting someone in front of a client, interrupting and using a nickname they dislike are all disrespectful.

q: A manager who explains why a change is needed, involves employees in planning it and celebrates early wins is
e: Leading change effectively means explaining why the change is needed, involving people in planning it and reinforcing progress by celebrating early wins. People resist change they don't understand or feel forced into, so communication and involvement increase buy-in.

q: The shared values, beliefs and behaviors that shape how employees work together in a company are its
e: Organizational culture is the shared values, beliefs and norms, 'the way we do things here,' that shape how people behave and work together. A mission statement is a written statement of purpose, the chain of command is the reporting structure, and bylaws are governance rules.

q: A team leader assigns the detail-oriented, analytical employee to check the numbers and the outgoing, people-oriented employee to present to the client. She is
e: Leveraging personality types means matching tasks to people's natural strengths: the analytical person checks numbers and the outgoing person presents. That improves results and job satisfaction. It's based on observed strengths, not favoritism or stereotyping.

q: Which is the most effective way to recognize an employee's contribution?
o: Give specific, timely praise that names what the employee did well
Wait until the annual review to mention it
Praise the whole department in general terms
Give a reward only when the employee asks
e: Recognition motivates most when it's specific (naming exactly what the person did well), sincere and timely (soon after the action). Waiting months, praising vaguely or only rewarding people who ask makes recognition feel generic or unfair.

q: What is the first step in the decision-making process?
o: Define the problem or decision to be made
e: Decision-making starts with clearly defining the problem or decision, because a vague or wrong problem leads to the wrong solution. The usual steps are: define the problem, gather information, list alternatives, evaluate them, choose, act and review the results.

q: A bank's online loan applications drop 30%. Before suggesting solutions, the team reviews website data and talks to customers. They are
o: gathering information to identify the cause of the problem.
e: Effective problem solving finds the root cause before jumping to solutions. Reviewing website data and talking to customers is gathering information to understand why applications dropped. Only then should the team brainstorm, choose and implement a fix.

q: Which is the best example of time management?
o: Ranking tasks by importance and due date, then doing the most important first
Doing the easiest tasks first to feel productive
e: Good time management means prioritizing: ranking tasks by importance and deadline and doing the most important work first. Constantly checking email interrupts focus, doing easy tasks first leaves important work undone, and saying yes to everything overloads you.

q: An accountant follows the same checklist every month to close the books so nothing is missed. She is demonstrating
e: Systematic behavior means working in an organized, step-by-step way so nothing is missed. A month-end closing checklist is a perfect example, and it reduces errors in financial records. Creativity is generating new ideas, and initiative is acting without being told.

q: Why does personal appearance matter for a financial advisor meeting a new client?
o: Clients form first impressions quickly, and a professional look builds trust
It is required by federal law
It replaces the need for product knowledge
It allows the advisor to charge higher fees
e: People form first impressions within seconds, and clients are deciding whether to trust you with their money. A professional appearance signals competence and seriousness, which helps build trust from the start. It isn't legally required and never replaces knowledge.

q: Which law sets the federal minimum wage and overtime pay rules for most U.S. workers?
e: The Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 sets the federal minimum wage (currently $7.25 an hour), overtime pay of 1.5 times regular pay over 40 hours for non-exempt workers, and child labor rules. Sarbanes-Oxley, Dodd-Frank and Gramm-Leach-Bliley are finance laws.

q: During a job interview for a bank analyst position, which response best answers "Tell me about a time you made a mistake"?
o: Describe a real mistake, what you did to fix it and what you learned
Say you have never made a mistake
Change the subject to your strengths
e: Interviewers ask about mistakes to see honesty, accountability and whether you learn. The best answer briefly describes a real mistake, how you fixed it and what you do differently now. Claiming you never err, blaming others or dodging the question are red flags.

q: Which belongs on a resume for a high school student applying for a bank internship?
o: DECA competition results and a part-time job with responsibilities and results
A photo and Social Security number
A list of every class taken since ninth grade
e: A resume should show relevant achievements and experience: DECA results show business knowledge and competitiveness, and a part-time job with responsibilities shows work ethic. Never include a Social Security number or photo, list every class or state salary expectations.

q: When should you send a thank-you or follow-up message after a job interview?
o: Only if you don't hear back in a month
Only if you got the job
e: A thank-you message within 24 hours of the interview shows professionalism and appreciation, and keeps you top of mind while the employer decides. Waiting a month or only following up if hired misses the chance to make a final good impression.

q: Which is the best example of networking to find a finance job?
o: Asking a family friend who is a CPA for an informational interview
Applying to 100 job postings without researching them
Waiting for employers to contact you
Posting complaints about your current job online
e: Networking means building relationships with people who can share advice, insight and job leads. An informational interview with a CPA family friend is a classic networking step. Mass-applying without research or waiting to be contacted isn't networking.

q: A student who wants to work in banking volunteers to help with a free tax-preparation program at a community center. She is
e: Volunteering, such as with a free tax-preparation program like VITA, gives real experience, skills and references before a first full-time job. It shows initiative and interest in the field. It isn't a certification or a job application.

q: Why is ongoing education important for finance professionals?
o: Laws, technology and products change, so skills must be updated
It guarantees a promotion every year
It is only needed for people who change careers
e: Finance changes constantly: new laws (like the 2025 tax law), new products and new technology. Many credentials, including the CFP, CPA and FINRA licenses, require continuing education so professionals stay current and give accurate advice. It doesn't guarantee promotions.

q: A bank creates a feature that rounds up every debit card purchase and moves the spare change into savings. This is an example of
e: Innovation means turning a new idea into a product, service or process that creates value. A round-up feature that automatically moves spare change into savings is a new way to help customers save. Consolidation is merging firms, and compliance is following rules.

q: Which is a SMART goal?
o: Save $1,200 for an emergency fund by June 30 by depositing $100 a month
Spend less on things I don't need
e: SMART goals are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound. 'Save $1,200 by June 30 by depositing $100 a month' has a clear amount, a deadline and a plan. 'Save more money' and 'become rich someday' are vague wishes with no measure or deadline.

q: Which job involves reviewing loan applications and deciding whether borrowers meet the lender's standards?
e: A loan underwriter reviews applications, including credit, income, debt and collateral, and decides whether the borrower meets the lender's standards and on what terms. Actuaries use statistics to measure risk, compliance officers ensure rules are followed and auditors check records.

q: Which professional uses statistics and math to calculate the probability and cost of future events for insurance companies?
e: Actuaries use math, statistics and data to estimate the probability and cost of future events like deaths, accidents and illnesses. Insurers use their work to set premiums and reserves. Underwriters then apply those guidelines to individual applicants.

q: Which credential is most closely associated with personal financial planning?
e: The Certified Financial Planner (CFP) credential is the best-known designation for personal financial planning, and CFP professionals must act as fiduciaries. CPAs specialize in accounting and tax, CFAs in investment analysis and CIAs in internal auditing.

q: A new financial advisor joins the local chamber of commerce and attends its monthly events. The main purpose is to
o: build relationships that can lead to referrals and clients
avoid having to make sales calls
e: Chambers of commerce and community groups put advisors in regular contact with local business owners and professionals. Building those relationships leads to trust, referrals and new clients over time, which is the main purpose of joining.

q: A company with strong corporate governance is most likely to
o: attract investors and borrow money at a lower cost
e: Investors and lenders see well-governed companies, those with independent boards, transparent reporting and strong controls, as lower risk. Lower perceived risk makes it easier to attract investors and borrow at lower interest rates. Governance doesn't exempt a company from regulation or taxes.

q: Which committee of the board of directors oversees the company's financial reporting and works with the external auditors?
e: The audit committee, made up entirely of independent directors at listed companies, oversees financial reporting, internal controls and the relationship with the external auditors. Sarbanes-Oxley strengthened its role. The compensation committee sets executive pay.

q: Having the CEO and the board chair be two different people is meant to
o: give the board independent oversight of management
e: The board's job is to oversee the CEO. If the CEO also chairs the board, they're essentially supervising themselves. Separating the roles, or naming a lead independent director, gives the board independence to challenge management and hold it accountable.

q: An employee who reports a suspected accounting violation through the company's ethics hotline is helping to
e: Governance objectives include ethical behavior and accurate financial reporting, and every employee plays a part. Reporting a suspected violation through the ethics hotline uses the channel the company created for exactly this. Most fraud is discovered through tips.

q: After a company adopts a policy requiring board approval for any purchase over $5 million, how is management most affected?
o: Major decisions take more review time but face more oversight
Managers can no longer make any decisions
The company no longer needs auditors
e: Approval thresholds are a governance process: managers still run the business, but the biggest decisions need board review. That adds some time but gives independent oversight of high-risk choices, reducing the chance of costly mistakes.

q: A loan officer nods, maintains eye contact and repeats the client's main concern back in her own words. She is practicing
e: Active listening means fully engaging with the speaker: paying attention, showing interest through eye contact and nodding, and paraphrasing to confirm you understood. Repeating the client's concern in her own words proves she heard it correctly and makes the client feel heard.

q: A client says "I'm fine with that plan" but crosses his arms and frowns. The advisor should
o: notice the mixed signal and ask what concerns he has
continue, because he said he was fine
point out that his body language is rude
e: When body language, such as crossed arms and a frown, contradicts words, the nonverbal signal often reveals true feelings. Asking an open question like 'What concerns do you have?' invites the client to share hesitations so the advisor can address them before moving forward.

q: An advisor explaining investments to a 19-year-old first-time investor should
o: use simple language and everyday examples, avoiding jargon
use technical terms to show expertise
give a printed prospectus and skip the explanation
e: Good communicators adapt to their audience. A first-time investor needs plain language and everyday examples, like comparing diversification to not putting all your eggs in one basket. Jargon or advanced strategies would confuse and discourage them.

q: When a judge challenges your recommendation, the best way to defend your idea objectively is to
o: calmly explain the facts and reasoning behind it and acknowledge valid concerns
e: Defending ideas objectively means staying calm, explaining the facts and reasoning behind your recommendation and acknowledging any valid points the judge raises. That shows confidence and critical thinking. Getting louder or dismissing the judge looks defensive, and instantly giving up looks unprepared.

q: Which is the best way to open a business presentation?
o: State the purpose and give a brief overview of what you will cover
Start with the details of your last point
Read the first slide word for word
e: A strong opening states the purpose and previews what you'll cover, so the audience knows why to listen and where you're going. In a roleplay that means a one-sentence recommendation and an agenda. Apologizing or reading slides weakens your credibility.

q: An analyst organizes a report from the most important finding to the least important. This organization is
e: Order of importance puts the most significant information first, so busy readers get the key points immediately even if they stop reading early. Chronological order follows time, spatial order follows physical layout and alphabetical order follows letters.

q: Which graphic aid is best for showing how a company's revenue changed over the last 10 years?
e: A line graph is best for trends over time: years go along the bottom, revenue up the side, and the line shows rises and falls clearly. Pie charts show parts of a whole at one moment, organizational charts show reporting structure and flowcharts show process steps.

q: A one-page summary at the start of a long report that gives decision makers the key findings and recommendations is a(n)
e: An executive summary condenses a long report's key findings and recommendations into a page at the front, so busy decision makers can act without reading everything. It must make sense on its own. An appendix holds supporting detail at the back, and a bibliography lists sources.

q: Which is a guideline for writing professional emails?
o: Use a clear subject line and keep the message brief and focused
Write in all capital letters for emphasis
Send sensitive client data in the body of the email
e: Professional emails should have a clear subject line and a brief, focused message so the reader knows immediately what it's about and what's needed. All caps reads as shouting, emojis can seem unprofessional with clients, and sensitive data should never go in an unencrypted email.

q: Which is the best practice for a financial advisor using social media?
o: Keep business accounts professional and follow the firm's compliance rules
Post client success stories with names and account balances
Share stock tips on a personal account
Use one account for both personal and business posts
e: Financial firms must follow FINRA and SEC rules on advertising and record-keeping for social media, and client information is confidential. Keeping business accounts professional and following the firm's compliance policies protects clients and the advisor. Posting client details or stock tips breaks those rules.

q: Compared with a phone call, a text message to a client is
o: fast and convenient but less suited to complex or sensitive topics
e: Texts are quick and convenient for simple updates, like confirming an appointment, but they lack tone of voice and room for discussion. Complex or sensitive topics, like bad news or detailed financial decisions, are better handled by phone or in person.

q: An analyst turns a spreadsheet of branch sales into a color-coded map that shows which branches are performing best. This is an example of
e: Data visualization turns numbers into visual formats, such as maps, charts and dashboards, so patterns are easy to see at a glance. A color-coded map instantly shows which branches lead. Normalization organizes databases, and an audit trail tracks transaction history.

q: A customer is angry that a check deposit is on hold. What should the employee do first?
o: Listen without interrupting and acknowledge the customer's frustration
Explain that it is bank policy and move on
Tell the customer to come back when calm
e: With an upset customer, the first step is to listen without interrupting and acknowledge their frustration. People calm down when they feel heard, and then they're ready to hear the explanation (hold policies protect against bad checks) and options. Quoting policy first escalates the conflict.

q: A client asks why the bank charges a fee for paper statements. The best way to interpret this policy is to
o: explain the reason for the fee and offer the free e-statement option
waive every fee the client asks about
e: Interpreting a policy well means explaining the reason behind it, such as printing and mailing costs, and offering an alternative, like free e-statements, so the customer can avoid the fee. 'That's just the rule' frustrates customers, and waiving every fee isn't sustainable.

q: Which action best helps a new financial advisor build rapport with a client?
o: Remembering details the client shared, such as their children's names and goals
Talking mostly about the advisor's own achievements
Rushing through the meeting to respect the client's time
Using as much industry jargon as possible
e: Rapport is a relationship of trust and comfort. Remembering personal details, like a client's children's names and goals, shows genuine interest in them as a person, not just as an account. Talking about yourself, rushing or using jargon pushes clients away.

q: A credit union calls members on their account anniversaries to review whether their accounts still meet their needs. The main goal is to
o: sell as many products as possible in one call
e: Regular, helpful check-ins show members the credit union cares about their needs, not just sales. That builds loyalty and long-term relationships, which are far more valuable than a single sale, because keeping a customer costs much less than finding a new one.

q: A bank advertises "We're here when life happens" and trains staff to help customers through big life events. This message is the bank's
e: A brand promise is what a company commits to deliver to customers in every interaction. 'We're here when life happens,' backed by staff trained to help during life events, is the experience the bank promises. A mission statement describes the organization's purpose more broadly.

q: When serving a client whose first language is not English, a bank employee should
o: speak clearly, avoid slang and offer translated materials if available
ask a family member to make decisions for the client
e: Adapting to language differences means speaking clearly and at a normal pace, avoiding slang and idioms, checking understanding and offering translated materials or interpreters. Speaking louder doesn't help understanding, and decisions must remain the client's own.

q: Which use of CRM data is unethical?
o: Selling clients' personal information to outside marketers without permission
Reminding clients of upcoming CD maturity dates
Noting a client's preferred contact method
Tracking which services a client already uses
e: Selling clients' personal information to outside marketers without permission violates their privacy and trust, and financial institutions must follow privacy laws like Gramm-Leach-Bliley. CD maturity reminders, noting contact preferences and tracking services serve the client.

q: A client says, "I don't trust advisors. You just want to sell me things." What is the best response?
o: Explain how you are paid, your duty to act in the client's best interest and how they can check your record
Tell the client most people feel that way and move on
Offer a discount on the first product
e: Trust comes from transparency. Explaining exactly how you're paid, your duty to act in the client's best interest and how they can verify your record on FINRA BrokerCheck addresses the concern directly. Guaranteeing returns is unethical, and discounts or brushing it off don't build trust.

q: A client's goals and risk tolerance must be understood before an advisor recommends investments. This requirement is known as
e: Know your customer (KYC) rules require firms to gather information about a client's identity, finances, goals and risk tolerance. Suitability, and for brokers Regulation Best Interest, requires recommendations to fit that profile. Churning is excessive trading for commissions, and front-running is trading ahead of client orders.

q: Which activity is part of a bank's operations function?
o: Processing deposits and loan payments accurately each day
Setting the Federal Reserve's interest rates
e: Operations are the day-to-day activities that produce and deliver a company's products and services. For a bank, that means accurately processing deposits, payments and loans. Advertising is marketing, the Fed sets policy rates and the mission statement comes from leadership.

q: Under the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, financial institutions must
o: explain their information-sharing practices to customers and protect sensitive data
guarantee every deposit up to $1 million
report all employee salaries to the public
e: The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (1999) requires financial institutions to give customers privacy notices explaining how they share information, to let customers opt out of some sharing, and to protect sensitive data with security safeguards. It doesn't guarantee deposits; FDIC insurance covers $250,000.

q: Requiring employees to use a password plus a code sent to their phone to log in is an example of
e: Multifactor authentication requires two or more kinds of proof: something you know (a password), something you have (a phone or security key) or something you are (a fingerprint). Even if a password is stolen, the attacker can't log in without the second factor.

q: An employee receives an email that looks like it's from IT asking for his password. He should
o: not reply and report it as a possible phishing attempt
click the link to check if it's real
e: Real IT departments never ask for passwords by email. This is a phishing attempt, a fake message designed to steal login credentials. The right response is not to reply or click anything and to report it to security so others can be warned.

q: A project has a defined scope, budget and deadline, and ends when the goal is reached. This describes
e: A project is temporary: it has a specific goal, scope, budget and deadline, and it ends when the goal is reached. Project management plans and controls that work. Ongoing operations, like processing daily deposits, continue indefinitely.

q: A bar chart showing project tasks along a timeline with their start and end dates is a
e: A Gantt chart lists project tasks down the side and shows each as a horizontal bar along a timeline, with start and end dates. It makes schedules, overlaps and progress easy to track. Pie charts show parts of a whole, and flowcharts show process steps.

q: A project is two weeks behind schedule. The project manager should first
o: identify the cause of the delay and adjust the plan
ignore it and hope the team catches up
e: Monitoring a project means comparing progress with the plan and taking corrective action. The manager should first find out why it's late, such as underestimated tasks, missing resources or scope changes, then adjust the plan by reassigning work or revising dates.

q: Which question best evaluates whether a project succeeded?
o: Did it meet its goals on time and within budget?
Did everyone enjoy working on it?
Was it the most expensive project of the year?
Did it use the newest software?
e: Project success is measured against the goals set at the start: did it deliver what was intended, on time and within budget? Whether people enjoyed it, how expensive it was or what software it used doesn't show whether it accomplished its purpose.

q: Which is a main goal of the purchasing function?
o: Getting the right goods at the right price, quality and time
e: Purchasing buys the goods and services a business needs on the best terms: the right items, at the right quality, price and quantity, delivered at the right time. Selling to customers is marketing and sales, hiring is HR and tax returns are accounting.

q: A purchasing agent accepts expensive gifts from a supplier and then gives that supplier a contract. This is unethical because it
e: Accepting expensive gifts and then awarding that supplier a contract creates a conflict of interest: the agent's personal benefit may have influenced a decision that should be based on price, quality and reliability. Many companies limit or ban vendor gifts for this reason.

q: When selecting a vendor, which factor is usually most important besides price?
o: How close the vendor's owner lives
How many ads the vendor runs
e: A vendor that is reliable and delivers good quality on time is often worth more than the cheapest option, because late or defective goods cause delays, rework and unhappy customers. Where the owner lives, logos and advertising don't affect value.

q: Which is an example of production in a service business such as a bank?
o: Creating and delivering a new mortgage loan for a customer
Building cars on an assembly line
e: Production means creating goods or services that satisfy customers. In a bank the products are financial services, so creating and delivering a mortgage is production. Mining, farming and assembly lines are production in goods industries.

q: In a company with a strong quality culture, employees
o: take responsibility for quality and are encouraged to report problems
leave quality to the inspection department
e: In a strong quality culture, quality is everyone's responsibility, not just inspectors'. Employees are encouraged to report problems without fear of blame, so issues get fixed early. Hiding errors or focusing only on speed leads to more defects and unhappy customers.

q: All the businesses and activities involved in getting a product from raw materials to the final customer make up the
e: The supply chain is the network of suppliers, manufacturers, distributors and retailers that moves a product from raw materials to the final customer. Disruptions anywhere in it, like the 2021-22 shortages, affect costs and availability. The chain of command is a reporting structure.

q: A bank cuts its account-opening process from 14 steps to 6 by removing duplicate forms. This is an example of
e: Streamlining a work process removes unnecessary or duplicate steps to make it faster, cheaper and less error-prone, and improves the customer experience. Cutting 14 steps to 6 by eliminating duplicate forms is a clear example. Outsourcing would hire another company to do the work.

q: Which is an overhead (operating) cost for a tax-preparation business?
e: Overhead costs keep the business running but aren't tied to a specific client or product. Office rent is a classic example, along with utilities and insurance. A service firm has little or no cost of goods sold, and owner investments and loan proceeds are financing, not expenses.

q: Because a city has limited money, it must choose between building a new park and repairing roads. This illustrates
e: Scarcity means resources are limited while wants are not, so choices must be made. If the city repairs roads, the park it gave up is the opportunity cost, the value of the next-best alternative. Every financial decision involves the same trade-off.

q: Money, buildings and equipment used to produce goods and services are which type of economic resource?
e: Capital is one of the four factors of production: tools, machinery, buildings and money used to produce goods and services. Land is natural resources, labor is human work, and entrepreneurship is organizing the other three and taking risk.

q: A bank opens a branch inside a grocery store so customers can bank where they already shop. This creates which economic utility?
e: Place utility is value created by making a product available where customers want it. A branch inside a grocery store puts banking where customers already are. Time utility is when it's available, form utility comes from changing a product's form, and possession utility from ease of ownership.

q: When prices rise because demand is high, producers are encouraged to make more. This shows the function of prices to
e: Prices act as signals in a market economy. High prices tell producers that customers want more and that making more could be profitable, motivating them to increase supply; low prices signal the opposite. This coordinates production without central planning.

q: An economic system in which individuals and businesses own resources and make most decisions based on supply and demand is a
e: In a market economy, also called free enterprise or capitalism, individuals and businesses own resources and decide what to produce based on supply, demand and prices. In a command economy the government makes those decisions, and in a traditional economy custom does.

q: Which is a key feature of private enterprise?
o: The right to own property and keep profits
Fixed prices set by the government
e: Private enterprise rests on property rights (owning businesses and assets), the profit motive (keeping what you earn), competition and freedom of choice. Government ownership, government-fixed prices and no competition describe a command economy.

q: Which is an example of an economic business risk?
o: A recession reduces demand for loans
A customer slips on a wet floor
e: Economic risks come from changes in the economy, such as recessions, inflation, interest rates and unemployment. A recession lowering loan demand is economic. An earthquake is a natural risk, and employee theft and a customer slip are human risks.

q: Several banks in a town lower fees and raise savings rates to attract customers. This is
e: Competition is rivalry among businesses for customers. Banks lowering fees and raising savings rates to win customers shows competition pushing firms to offer better value. A monopoly has no competitors, and price fixing is an illegal agreement to set prices.

q: How does high inflation usually affect savers who keep money in a regular savings account earning 1%?
o: Their interest rate automatically rises to match inflation
e: If inflation is 4% and savings earn 1%, the money grows 1% but prices rise 4%, so it buys about 3% less each year. That loss of real purchasing power is why savers need returns above inflation. Savings account rates don't automatically match inflation.

q: When the Federal Reserve raises interest rates, what usually happens?
o: Borrowing becomes more expensive and spending slows
e: When the Fed raises rates, banks charge more for loans, credit cards and mortgages, so borrowing becomes more expensive. People and businesses borrow and spend less, which slows the economy and cools inflation. Savers usually earn more, not less.

q: The total value of all final goods and services produced in a country in one year is
e: Gross domestic product (GDP) measures the total value of all final goods and services produced in a country in a year. It's the main measure of economic output, and GDP = consumption + investment + government spending + net exports. CPI measures changes in consumer prices.

q: Which is most likely when unemployment rises sharply?
e: When people lose jobs, they lose income and become cautious, so consumer spending falls. Since spending is about two-thirds of U.S. GDP, the economy slows further. High unemployment usually pushes inflation and interest rates down, not up.

q: If the U.S. dollar strengthens against the euro, what happens to U.S. companies that export to Europe?
o: Their products become more expensive for European buyers
Their products become cheaper for European buyers
e: When the dollar strengthens, each euro buys fewer dollars, so a product priced at $100 costs Europeans more euros than before. That makes U.S. exports more expensive and harder to sell in Europe, while European imports become cheaper for Americans.

q: Which is an external factor affecting a bank's business environment?
e: External factors come from outside the company: economic, political, legal, social and technological changes such as new federal banking regulations. The bank can respond but can't control them. Training programs, office layout and the mission statement are internal.

q: An analyst is researching interest-rate trends. Which source is most reliable?
o: A blog with no author or date
e: Reliable sources have authority, accuracy and current dates. The Federal Reserve's official website publishes actual interest-rate data and policy decisions, so it's authoritative. Anonymous posts, undated blogs and forum comments have no accountability or verified accuracy.

q: What is the most efficient first step when searching for information online?
o: Use specific keywords that describe exactly what you need
Read every result on the first five pages
e: Specific keywords that describe exactly what you need narrow results to relevant pages quickly. For example, '2027 401(k) contribution limit IRS' beats 'retirement.' Reading every result wastes time, single common words return too much, and ads are paid placements.

q: After analyzing data, an analyst finds that branches with longer wait times have lower customer satisfaction. What should she conclude?
o: There is a relationship worth investigating, but it doesn't prove wait times alone cause low satisfaction
Wait times definitely cause all dissatisfaction
e: This is correlation: the two things move together. It doesn't prove that wait times alone cause dissatisfaction, since other factors like staffing or location might affect both. The right conclusion is that the relationship is worth investigating further.

q: Why is information management important to a business?
o: It ensures the right information is available to the right people for decisions
It eliminates the need for employees
It replaces all paper records with the internet
e: Information management collects, organizes, protects and delivers information so the right people have the right information at the right time to make decisions. It also supports legal compliance and reduces risk. It doesn't replace employees or guarantee sales.

q: Which is a legal issue associated with information management in finance?
o: Protecting customers' personal financial data under privacy laws
Choosing the color of a website
Deciding the length of a meeting
e: Financial institutions must protect customers' personal financial data under privacy and security laws such as the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, and data breaches can lead to fines and lawsuits. Website colors, meeting length and furniture aren't legal issues.

q: Which is a way technology has changed banking?
o: Customers can deposit checks by taking a photo with a mobile app
Customers must visit a branch for every transaction
Interest rates are now set by computers
e: Mobile check deposit lets customers deposit a check by photographing it in their bank's app, with no branch visit. Along with online banking and instant payments, it shows how technology has made banking faster and more convenient. Banks need more security, not less.

q: In a spreadsheet, which formula adds the values in cells B2 through B10?
e: =SUM(B2:B10) adds every value in the range B2 through B10; the colon means 'through.' There's no ADD or TOTAL function in standard spreadsheets, and =B2:B10 alone doesn't calculate a sum.

q: A spreadsheet feature that shows only the rows meeting certain conditions, such as loans over $50,000, is
e: Filtering temporarily hides rows that don't meet your criteria, such as loans over $50,000, so you see only the relevant data. Formatting changes appearance, merging combines cells and freezing panes keeps headers visible while scrolling.

q: In a database, each row that contains all the information about one customer is called a
e: A record is one row containing all the information about one item, such as one customer. A field is one column, a single type of information like phone number. A table holds many records, and a query retrieves records that match criteria.

q: An analyst calculates the middle value in a list of loan amounts sorted from smallest to largest. She is finding the
e: The median is the middle value when numbers are sorted, with half above and half below. It's less distorted by extreme values than the mean (average). For loan amounts, a few huge loans can pull the mean up while the median stays representative.

q: Analyzing large amounts of data to discover hidden patterns, such as which customers are likely to close their accounts, is
e: Data mining uses software and statistical methods to search large data sets for hidden patterns and relationships, such as signs a customer is likely to close an account. Banks use it to predict behavior and act early. Data entry and bookkeeping just record data.

q: Which is a current trend in financial services?
o: Using artificial intelligence to detect fraud and answer customer questions
e: Artificial intelligence is a major current trend in finance: banks use it to detect fraud in real time, power chatbots like Bank of America's Erica and support lending decisions. Digital banking is growing, not disappearing.

q: A person who takes on the risk of starting a new business in hopes of making a profit is a(n)
e: An entrepreneur organizes resources and accepts the financial risk of starting a business in hopes of earning a profit. Employees work for wages, shareholders own part of an existing company and creditors lend money.

q: Which is a role requirement of a small-business owner?
o: Making final decisions and accepting responsibility for the business's results
Working only the hours stated in a contract
e: A small-business owner makes final decisions and is responsible for the results, good or bad, including finances, legal obligations, employees and customers. Owners don't have guaranteed salaries or fixed hours, and they don't follow a manager's instructions.

q: A start-up founder tells investors her app has 50,000 users when it actually has 5,000. This is
e: Telling investors you have 50,000 users when you have 5,000 is a material misrepresentation, a lie about a fact investors rely on. It's unethical and can be securities fraud. Honest pitches can be optimistic about the future but must be truthful about the facts.

q: A small U.S. company that sells handmade goods online to customers in Canada and Japan is taking advantage of
e: Selling to customers in other countries is international trade. E-commerce platforms and global shipping let even very small businesses reach buyers worldwide. Protectionism, embargoes and quotas are barriers that restrict trade.

q: Which is a major way small businesses help a market economy?
o: They create jobs and introduce new ideas and competition
They eliminate the need for large companies
e: Small businesses make up about 99.9% of U.S. businesses and employ nearly half of private-sector workers (SBA). They create jobs, bring new ideas to market and compete with larger firms, which keeps prices and quality in check. They don't set interest rates or prevent inflation.

q: Which activity is a main responsibility of human resources management?
e: Human resources management handles the people side of a business: recruiting, hiring, training, pay and benefits, performance reviews and employee relations. Approving loans is a banking function, managing investments is finance and designing ads is marketing.

q: An HR manager learns that two candidates are equally qualified and chooses the one who went to her college. Why is this an ethical problem?
o: The decision is based on personal bias, not job-related qualifications
It is illegal to hire college graduates
HR managers cannot make hiring decisions
e: Choosing a candidate because she went to the same college is a personal bias, not a job-related reason. Ethical, fair hiring uses consistent criteria tied to the job. Favoritism like this can also create a less diverse workforce and legal risk.

q: A company uses software that tracks employee hours, benefits and performance reviews in one system. This is an example of
o: using technology in human resources management.
e: A human resource information system (HRIS) puts payroll, hours, benefits and performance records in one system, automating paperwork and improving accuracy. It's a technology tool for HR. CRM software manages customers, not employees.

q: Which is a main purpose of new-employee orientation?
o: Helping new hires understand the company's policies, culture and their role
Evaluating whether to fire the employee
e: Orientation introduces new hires to the company's policies, culture, people and their own role, so they feel welcome and become productive faster. Good orientation lowers early turnover. It doesn't evaluate firing, set lifetime pay or replace job training.

q: Which is the best description of marketing?
o: Creating, communicating and delivering value to customers
e: Marketing is the process of creating, communicating and delivering value to customers. It includes research, product decisions, pricing, distribution, promotion and selling. Advertising is just one part, and manufacturing and record-keeping belong to other functions.

q: A bank studies which age groups use its mobile app. This is which marketing function?
e: Marketing-information management gathers and analyzes data about customers and markets, such as who uses the app, to guide marketing decisions. Channel management deals with distribution, pricing sets prices and selling is direct communication with customers.

q: Which employee action best helps a bank achieve its goal of increasing customer satisfaction?
o: Following up with customers to make sure their problem was solved
Rushing customers to reduce wait times at any cost
Recommending products the customer doesn't need
e: Following up to confirm a customer's problem was solved shows care and directly raises satisfaction. Rushing customers, avoiding difficult ones or pushing unneeded products all hurt satisfaction, even if they seem efficient in the moment.

q: After a bank adds Saturday hours, new account openings rise 15%. This is an example of
o: a connection between a company action and its results.
e: Businesses measure how their decisions affect results. Adding Saturday hours (an action) followed by a 15% rise in account openings (a result) shows a connection between them, which tells the bank the change worked. It isn't an external factor because the bank chose it.

q: The management function of setting goals and deciding how to achieve them is
e: Planning sets goals and decides how to reach them: strategies, budgets and timelines. It comes first. Organizing arranges people and resources, staffing hires and trains people and controlling compares results with the plan.

q: Buying insurance to cover possible losses is which risk-management strategy?
e: Buying insurance transfers the financial risk of a loss to the insurance company in exchange for a premium. The four main strategies are avoid (don't do it), reduce or control (lower the chance or impact), transfer (insurance or contracts) and retain (accept it and pay losses yourself).

q: A bank decides not to offer cryptocurrency trading because the risks are too high. This strategy is
e: Risk avoidance means choosing not to take part in a risky activity at all. By not offering crypto trading, the bank removes that risk entirely, but also gives up any potential revenue. Transferring would mean insuring it, and retaining would mean accepting it.

q: When conducting a risk assessment for a company event, what should be done after identifying possible risks?
o: Estimate how likely each risk is and how severe its impact would be
Buy insurance for every possible risk
e: After identifying risks, the next step is to assess each one: how likely is it, and how severe would the impact be? Ranking risks on a likelihood-times-impact matrix shows which deserve attention and money first. Canceling everything or insuring every risk isn't practical.

q: Which is an external factor that can affect how a bank is managed?
o: Changes in interest rates set by the Federal Reserve
The layout of the bank's lobby
e: External factors come from outside the organization, such as the economy, laws, competitors and technology. Federal Reserve interest-rate changes directly affect what a bank pays depositors and charges borrowers. Dress codes, lobby layout and leadership style are internal.

q: Why should a young worker start investing for retirement as early as possible?
o: Compound growth has more years to work
Early investments are guaranteed not to lose value
Taxes on investments are lower for young people
Retirement accounts close to people over 30
e: Starting early gives compound growth more years to work, as earnings earn their own returns. $200 a month from 22 to 65 at 8% grows to about $895,000, but starting at 32 gives about $387,000. No investment is guaranteed, and retirement accounts have no age cutoff.

q: Which is the main reason to keep an emergency fund in a savings account rather than in stocks?
o: The money must be available quickly without risk of loss
Savings accounts earn higher long-term returns than stocks
Emergency funds are taxed less in savings
e: An emergency fund must be available immediately and stable in value. Stocks can fall 20% or more right when you lose a job or face a big bill, forcing you to sell at a loss. An insured savings account keeps the money liquid and safe; stocks are for long-term goals.

q: Setting up an automatic transfer from each paycheck into savings before paying other expenses is called
e: Paying yourself first means saving before you pay bills or spend, usually by automatic transfer on payday. Because the money moves automatically, saving happens without relying on willpower. Dollar-cost averaging is investing a fixed amount on a schedule, a related idea.

q: Investing the same dollar amount in a fund every month, regardless of price, is called
e: Dollar-cost averaging invests a fixed dollar amount on a regular schedule regardless of price. The same $300 buys more shares when prices are low and fewer when they're high, and it removes the temptation to time the market. Market timing tries to buy low and sell high, which rarely works.

q: Which investment pools money from many investors and tracks a market index, such as the S&P 500, at a low cost?
e: An index fund, a mutual fund or ETF, pools investors' money and holds the stocks in an index such as the S&P 500. It offers instant diversification across hundreds of companies at very low fees, often under 0.10% a year. CDs and bonds are single debt investments.

q: Which investment generally has the highest risk and the highest potential long-term return?
e: Stocks are ownership in companies, so their value rises and falls with profits and the economy. That makes them the most volatile of these choices, but over long periods they've earned the most, about 10% a year for the S&P 500 since 1928. CDs, T-bills and savings are safer but earn less.

q: When you buy a bond, you are
o: lending money to the issuer in exchange for interest
e: A bond is a loan from the investor to a government or company. The issuer pays interest (the coupon) and repays the face value at maturity. Bondholders are creditors, not owners; buying stock makes you an owner.

q: Spreading money across stocks, bonds and cash so that one bad investment doesn't ruin a portfolio is
e: Diversification spreads money across different investments that don't all move together, so a loss in one is cushioned by others. It lowers risk without giving up much return. Leverage is borrowing to invest, which increases risk.

q: A fund that automatically shifts from mostly stocks to more bonds as a chosen retirement year approaches is a
e: A target-date fund is named for a retirement year, such as 2065, and automatically shifts from mostly stocks to more bonds as that year approaches, becoming more conservative over time. It's a simple one-fund choice and a common 401(k) default.

q: A real estate investment trust (REIT) lets an investor
o: own a share of a portfolio of income-producing properties
buy a single home with no down payment
borrow money at a fixed rate
e: A REIT owns income-producing properties, like apartments, offices, warehouses or malls, and sells shares to investors, who get a slice of the rental income. REITs must pay out at least 90% of taxable income as dividends. They still carry market risk.

q: Saving for a house down payment in four years is which type of financial goal?
e: Financial goals are grouped by time: short-term (under about a year), medium-term (about 1 to 5 years) and long-term (more than 5 years). A down payment in four years is medium-term, so the money belongs in safer choices like high-yield savings, CDs or Treasuries, not mostly stocks.

q: Using the Rule of 72, about how long will it take money to double at an 8% annual return?
e: The Rule of 72 estimates doubling time: divide 72 by the annual return. 72 / 8 = 9 years. It's a quick way to show clients the power of compounding, and why moving from a 4% to an 8% return can cut doubling time from 18 to 9 years.

q: You deposit $5,000 at 4% interest compounded annually. How much will you have after 2 years?
e: Compound interest earns interest on interest. Year 1: $5,000 x 1.04 = $5,200. Year 2: $5,200 x 1.04 = $5,408. Simple interest would give $5,400; the extra $8 is interest earned on year 1's $200 of interest.

q: Simple interest on $3,000 at 5% per year for 3 years is
e: Simple interest = principal x rate x time = $3,000 x 0.05 x 3 = $450. Simple interest is calculated only on the original principal, never on interest already earned. $3,450 would be the total balance, not the interest.

q: An employer matches 100% of employee 401(k) contributions up to 4% of salary. An employee earning $50,000 contributes 4%. How much does the employer add per year?
e: The employee contributes 4% of $50,000 = $2,000. A 100% match up to 4% means the employer adds the same $2,000, for $4,000 total a year. That match is an instant 100% return, which is why getting the full match is usually step one in any savings plan.

q: What is the main tax difference between a Roth IRA and a traditional IRA?
o: Roth contributions are made after tax and qualified withdrawals are tax-free
Roth contributions are tax-deductible and withdrawals are taxed
Only Roth IRAs can hold stocks
e: With a Roth IRA you contribute money that's already been taxed, and qualified withdrawals in retirement, including all the growth, are tax-free. A traditional IRA may give a deduction now, but withdrawals are taxed later. Both can hold stocks.

q: Which account offers tax-free growth when the money is used for qualified education expenses?
e: A 529 plan is a state-sponsored education savings account. Earnings grow free of federal tax, and withdrawals are tax-free when used for qualified education expenses such as tuition, books, and room and board, plus K-12 tuition and some apprenticeships. Many states add a tax deduction.

q: A legal document that states how a person's property should be distributed after death is a
e: A will directs who receives your property after death, names an executor to carry it out and can name a guardian for minor children. A power of attorney lets someone act for you while you're alive, and it ends at death. A deed transfers title to real estate.

q: Kendra has $18,000 in assets and owes $11,000 on a car loan and credit cards. Her net worth is
e: Net worth = assets - liabilities = $18,000 - $11,000 = $7,000. It's a snapshot of financial position: what you'd have if you sold everything and paid every debt. Tracking it over time shows whether you're making progress.

q: Under the 50/30/20 budgeting guideline, what share of after-tax income goes to savings and paying down debt?
e: The 50/30/20 guideline splits after-tax income into 50% for needs (housing, food, insurance), 30% for wants (dining out, entertainment) and 20% for savings and extra debt payments. It's a simple starting framework that can be adjusted.

q: On a pay stub, the amount left after taxes and other deductions are subtracted is
e: Net pay, or take-home pay, is what's left after taxes (federal, state, Social Security, Medicare) and other deductions (health insurance, 401(k)) are subtracted from gross pay. Gross pay is total earnings before deductions, and budgets should be built on net pay.

q: Which tax is withheld from paychecks to fund Social Security and Medicare?
e: FICA (Federal Insurance Contributions Act) taxes fund Social Security (6.2% of wages up to the wage base) and Medicare (1.45% of all wages). Employers pay a matching amount. Sales, property and excise taxes aren't withheld from paychecks.

q: Which habit does the most to help a person build a good credit score?
o: Opening many new credit cards at once
Using the full credit limit every month
e: Payment history is the largest factor in a FICO score, about 35%, so paying every bill on time does the most for your score. Opening many cards at once adds hard inquiries, maxing out cards raises utilization, and closing your oldest card shortens your credit history.

q: A credit card has a $2,000 limit and a $1,500 balance. What is the credit utilization rate?
e: Credit utilization = balance / credit limit = $1,500 / $2,000 = 0.75, or 75%. High utilization signals heavy reliance on credit and lowers your score. Keeping it under 30%, and ideally under 10%, helps.

q: How can consumers check their credit reports from the three major bureaus for free?
o: By paying a credit repair company
Only by applying for a loan
e: AnnualCreditReport.com is the only official site, authorized by federal law, for free credit reports from Equifax, Experian and TransUnion, now available weekly. Credit repair companies charge for what you can do free, and checking your own report never hurts your score.

q: A $1,000 loan for one year costs $120 in interest and $30 in fees. What is the total finance charge?
e: The finance charge is the total cost of credit in dollars, including interest and fees: $120 + $30 = $150. The Truth in Lending Act requires lenders to disclose it along with the APR. $1,150 would be the total repaid, not the cost of borrowing.

q: Paying off debts from the highest interest rate to the lowest, while making minimum payments on the rest, is the
e: The avalanche method makes minimum payments on all debts and puts every extra dollar toward the highest-interest debt first, which saves the most interest overall. The snowball method pays the smallest balance first for quick motivational wins.

q: Which action best protects against identity theft?
o: Freezing your credit with the three bureaus
Using the same password for every account
Carrying your Social Security card in your wallet
Sharing account numbers on social media
e: A credit freeze at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion stops anyone from opening new credit in your name. It's free, doesn't affect your score and can be lifted temporarily when you apply for credit. Reusing passwords, carrying your Social Security card or posting account numbers all increase risk.

q: The Truth in Lending Act requires lenders to
o: disclose the APR and total finance charges before a loan is made
offer the lowest rate in the market
e: The Truth in Lending Act (1968) requires lenders to clearly disclose the cost of credit, including the APR and total finance charge, before you sign, so you can compare offers. It doesn't require the lowest rate, approval of every application or interest-free loans.

q: Which document will a lender most likely request when you apply for a car loan?
o: Proof of income, such as recent pay stubs
e: Lenders need to verify capacity, your ability to repay, so they ask for proof of income such as recent pay stubs, W-2s or tax returns, and they check your credit report. School transcripts, medical records and lists of friends aren't relevant to repaying a car loan.

q: A couple with a new baby depends on both of their incomes. Which insurance need should they review first?
e: When a family depends on both incomes, losing either parent would cause a serious financial loss. Life insurance on both parents, often term life of 10 to 12 times income, replaces that income so the child is protected. A new baby is a key life event that triggers an insurance review.

q: Which insurance replaces part of your income if an illness or injury keeps you from working?
e: Disability insurance pays a portion of your income, often 60% to 70%, if illness or injury keeps you from working. About 1 in 4 of today's 20-year-olds will become disabled before retirement age (SSA). Liability insurance covers harm to others, and life insurance pays at death.

q: An inexpensive policy that adds extra liability protection above home and auto coverage is
e: Umbrella insurance adds liability coverage, often $1 million or more, above the limits of your home and auto policies, protecting against large lawsuits. It usually costs a few hundred dollars a year, making it an inexpensive way to protect your assets.

q: The amount a policyholder must pay out of pocket before insurance begins to pay a claim is the
e: The deductible is what you pay out of pocket on a claim before insurance pays the rest. With a $1,000 deductible and a $5,000 loss, you pay $1,000 and the insurer pays $4,000. The premium is the regular price of the policy, and a beneficiary receives a life insurance payout.

q: Choosing a higher deductible on an insurance policy usually
o: has no effect on the premium
e: With a higher deductible you pay more of each loss yourself, so the insurer's expected costs fall and it charges a lower premium. It's a good trade-off when your emergency fund can cover the higher deductible.

q: Which type of life insurance lasts your whole life and builds cash value?
e: Whole (permanent) life insurance covers you for life and builds a cash value you can borrow against. Because of that, its premiums are much higher than term life for the same death benefit. Term covers a set period with no cash value.

q: The FDIC insures deposits at member banks up to
o: $250,000 per depositor, per bank, per ownership category
the full amount with no limit
e: FDIC insurance covers $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category, such as individual, joint or retirement accounts, so careful titling can insure more at one bank. The NCUA gives the same coverage at credit unions. No depositor has lost insured funds since 1934.

q: Which statement about credit unions compared with banks is most accurate?
o: Credit unions are member-owned not-for-profits and often have lower loan rates
Credit unions are owned by outside shareholders
Credit union deposits are not insured
e: Credit unions are not-for-profit cooperatives owned by their members, so earnings go back to members as lower loan rates, higher savings rates and fewer fees. Deposits are insured up to $250,000 by the NCUA, and they make loans like banks do.

q: Which organization protects customers' securities and cash if their brokerage firm fails?
e: SIPC (Securities Investor Protection Corporation) protects customers if a brokerage firm fails, up to $500,000, including $250,000 in cash. It doesn't cover losses from falling markets. The FDIC insures bank deposits, the SEC regulates markets and FINRA oversees brokers.

q: A company sells new shares of stock to the public for the first time in the
o: primary market through an initial public offering (IPO).
e: When a company sells new shares to the public for the first time, it's an initial public offering in the primary market, and the money goes to the company. Afterward, investors trade those shares with each other in the secondary market.

q: Which market is used for long-term borrowing and investing, such as stocks and bonds that last longer than a year?
e: The capital market handles long-term funds through stocks and bonds that last longer than a year, which pay for things like factories and infrastructure. The money market handles short-term debt of a year or less, such as T-bills and commercial paper.

q: A U.S. company exchanges dollars for euros to pay a supplier in Germany. This takes place in the
e: Currencies are bought and sold in the foreign exchange (forex) market, the largest financial market in the world at about $9.6 trillion a day (BIS, 2025). Paying a German supplier in euros requires converting dollars there. Stocks and bonds trade in other markets.

q: A long period in which stock prices fall 20% or more from their peak is called a
e: A bear market is a decline of 20% or more from a recent peak, often lasting months. A correction is a smaller drop of about 10%, a bull market is a long rise and a rally is a short-term rise.

q: When interest rates rise, what generally happens to the prices of existing bonds?
e: When rates rise, new bonds pay higher interest, so older bonds with lower fixed rates are less attractive. Their prices fall until their yield matches the market. This inverse relationship caused bond funds to drop about 13% in 2022.

q: An investor buys shares of a Japanese company on a U.S. exchange through an American depositary receipt (ADR). The main added risk is
o: currency risk from changes in the yen-dollar exchange rate
e: An ADR's value is tied to the Japanese company's shares, priced in yen. If the yen weakens against the dollar, the investment is worth fewer dollars even if the stock price in yen is unchanged. That's currency (exchange-rate) risk, the main added risk of foreign investing.

q: The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act of 1999 allowed
o: banks, securities firms and insurance companies to combine under one company
e: The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act repealed parts of the Glass-Steagall Act, allowing banks, securities firms and insurance companies to combine under one holding company. That enabled financial convergence, like Citigroup. It also added privacy and data-protection rules. The FDIC was created in 1933.

q: A company has current assets of $90,000 and current liabilities of $60,000. What is its current ratio?
e: Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities = $90,000 / $60,000 = 1.5. The company has $1.50 of short-term assets for every $1 of short-term debt, generally a comfortable level of liquidity. Below 1.0 would suggest trouble paying bills due within a year.

q: A business has revenue of $400,000, cost of goods sold of $240,000 and operating expenses of $100,000. What is its net income before taxes?
e: Work down the income statement. Gross profit = revenue - COGS = $400,000 - $240,000 = $160,000. Net income before taxes = gross profit - operating expenses = $160,000 - $100,000 = $60,000. $160,000 is gross profit, a common trap answer.

q: A budget that starts from zero each year and requires every expense to be justified is a
e: Zero-based budgeting starts every budget at $0, so managers must justify every expense instead of just adding a percentage to last year's numbers (incremental budgeting). It forces a fresh look at whether each cost is still needed, though it takes more time.

q: Break-even point in units = fixed costs ÷ (price per unit − variable cost per unit). A food truck has $30,000 in fixed costs, sells meals for $12 and has $7 in variable cost per meal. How many meals must it sell to break even?
e: Each meal contributes $12 - $7 = $5 toward fixed costs (the contribution margin). To cover $30,000 of fixed costs: $30,000 / $5 = 6,000 meals. Below 6,000 the truck loses money; every meal after that adds $5 of profit.

q: A financial manager delays recording expenses so this quarter's profit looks better before a loan review. This is
o: an acceptable way to manage earnings.
e: Pushing expenses into a later period makes this quarter's profit look better than it really is. Doing it to impress a lender misleads the people relying on the numbers. It violates accrual accounting and finance ethics, and can be fraud.

q: Generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) in the United States are set by the
e: The Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB), a private, independent body, sets U.S. GAAP, and the SEC requires public companies to follow it. The IASB sets international standards (IFRS). The Federal Reserve, IRS and FDIC have other roles.

q: Which is a key benefit of cloud-based accounting software for a small business?
o: The owner and accountant can see up-to-date records from anywhere
It removes the need for any record keeping
It guarantees the business will be profitable
e: Cloud accounting software such as QuickBooks Online or Xero stores the books online and connects to bank feeds, so the owner and accountant both see up-to-date records from anywhere. It doesn't remove the need for record keeping, guarantee profit or eliminate cybersecurity risk.

q: A company's net income is $50,000 on revenue of $500,000. What is its net profit margin?
e: Net profit margin = net income / revenue = $50,000 / $500,000 = 0.10, or 10%. The company keeps 10 cents of profit from every dollar of sales after all expenses. Comparing margins with competitors shows how efficiently it operates.

q: Return on equity (ROE) measures
o: how much profit a company generates with the owners' investment
how much cash is on hand
e: Return on equity = net income / shareholders' equity. It shows how much profit the company earns for each dollar the owners have invested. Higher ROE means owners' money is used more effectively, though very high ROE can also come from heavy debt.

q: A company's debt-to-equity ratio rises from 0.5 to 2.0 over three years. What does this most likely mean?
o: The company now relies much more on borrowed money and is riskier
The company paid off its debt
e: Debt-to-equity = total liabilities / equity. Rising from 0.5 to 2.0 means the company went from 50 cents of debt per dollar of equity to $2. It relies much more on borrowed money, so required interest payments are larger and financial risk is higher.

q: Before deciding to open a new branch, a manager uses budgeting software to see what profit would look like if sales were 10% lower or 10% higher than expected. This is
e: Scenario (what-if) analysis changes key assumptions, like sales 10% lower or higher, to see how results would change. It shows the range of outcomes and whether the branch still makes sense in a bad case. A variance report compares actual to budget after the fact.

q: Which technology helps finance teams detect unusual transactions in real time?
e: Machine-learning fraud detection learns what normal transactions look like and flags unusual ones, such as odd amounts, locations or timing, as they happen. Paper ledgers, fax machines and monthly printouts can't analyze transactions in real time.

q: An accountant is asked by her manager to classify a personal expense as a business expense. The most ethical response is to
o: refuse and explain it would misstate the financial records
do it because the manager asked
do it but keep a private note
ask a coworker to do it instead
e: Recording a personal expense as a business expense misstates the financial records and can be fraud, including tax fraud. The ethical response is to refuse and explain why, and to escalate if pressured. Doing it, or having a coworker do it, makes her part of the misconduct.

q: A company reports how much water and energy it saves along with its financial results. This is an example of
o: a non-traditional use of financial information (sustainability reporting).
e: Sustainability (ESG) reporting connects environmental and social results, such as water and energy use and emissions, to financial performance. It's a non-traditional use of financial information. Cash flow statements, variance analyses and balance sheets are traditional financial reports.

q: Which is a responsibility of the financial-information management function?
o: Collecting, analyzing and reporting financial data for decision-making
Setting the Federal Reserve's interest rate
e: The financial-information management function collects, organizes, analyzes and reports financial data so managers, investors and regulators can make decisions. Logo design is marketing, hiring is HR and the Federal Reserve sets its own rates.

q: A lender reviews a client's debt-to-income ratio. If the client earns $6,000 a month and has $2,100 in monthly debt payments, the ratio is
e: Debt-to-income = monthly debt payments / gross monthly income = $2,100 / $6,000 = 0.35, or 35%. Many lenders prefer total DTI at or below about 36%, and some mortgage programs allow up to about 43%. A lower DTI means more room in the budget to handle new debt.

q: A bank requires employees to take at least one week of consecutive vacation each year so someone else handles their work. The main purpose is to
o: uncover fraud that requires daily attention to hide
e: Many fraud schemes need daily attention to hide, such as moving money between accounts. When the employee is away and someone else does the job, the scheme is likely to be discovered. That's why mandatory vacation is a classic internal control in banks; it caught the $53 million Dixon, Illinois, theft.

q: Which is an example of an external risk to a bank?
o: A sudden rise in interest rates
e: External risks come from outside the organization, such as interest-rate changes, recessions, new regulations and natural disasters. A sudden rate rise affects a bank's funding costs and bond values. Data-entry errors, broken machines and weak hiring are internal risks.

q: Under enterprise risk management, a company's risk appetite is
o: the amount and type of risk it is willing to accept to reach its goals
the total value of its insurance policies
the number of risks it has eliminated
e: Risk appetite is the amount and type of risk an organization is willing to accept in pursuit of its goals. Leaders set it, and it guides which risks to take, reduce or avoid across the company. A growth-focused startup may have a high appetite; a bank holding deposits a lower one.

q: The COSO framework is widely used to guide
o: internal control and enterprise risk management
e: COSO (Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission) publishes the most widely used frameworks for internal control (2013) and enterprise risk management (2017). Public companies commonly use COSO to meet Sarbanes-Oxley internal control requirements.

q: A bank runs a simulated ransomware attack to see how quickly employees respond. This is an example of
o: using technology to test and strengthen risk controls.
e: A simulated attack tests how well technology and people respond, revealing weaknesses like slow detection or unclear procedures before a real attack exploits them. It's using technology to test and strengthen risk controls. An external audit reviews financial statements.

q: Which law requires the CEO and CFO of a public company to personally certify the accuracy of financial reports?
e: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 requires the CEO and CFO to personally certify that financial reports are accurate (Section 302), with criminal penalties for knowingly false certification (Section 906). It was passed after the Enron and WorldCom frauds.

q: A financial firm discovers a data breach. Which action is most ethical?
o: Notify affected customers promptly and help them protect their accounts
Wait to see if anyone notices
Blame a vendor publicly before investigating
e: Ethical risk management means being transparent and protecting the people affected. Promptly notifying customers lets them change passwords, freeze credit and watch accounts, and most states legally require breach notification. Hiding it, deleting evidence or blaming others is unethical and often illegal.

q: Which agency regulates the securities industry and enforces federal securities laws?
e: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), created by the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, regulates securities markets, requires public companies to disclose information and enforces securities laws. FINRA oversees brokers under SEC supervision. The FDIC insures bank deposits.

q: A broker makes excessive trades in a client's account mainly to earn commissions. This illegal practice is
e: Churning is excessive trading in a client's account mainly to generate commissions for the broker. It puts the broker's interest ahead of the client's and racks up costs, so it's illegal. Diversifying and rebalancing are legitimate strategies that serve the client.

q: Which agency was created by the Dodd-Frank Act to protect consumers in financial products such as mortgages and credit cards?
e: The Dodd-Frank Act (2010), passed after the 2008 financial crisis, created the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) to protect consumers in mortgages, credit cards, student loans and other financial products. The Federal Reserve dates from 1913, and FINRA and SIPC are separate organizations.

q: Under Regulation Best Interest, a broker-dealer recommending an investment to a retail customer must
o: act in the customer's best interest and not put its own interest first
guarantee the investment will make money
e: Regulation Best Interest (2020) requires broker-dealers recommending investments to retail customers to act in the customer's best interest, without putting their own interest first, and to disclose and manage conflicts. It doesn't require guaranteed returns, the cheapest product or no commissions.

q: Which retirement account lets an employee contribute pre-tax money directly from a paycheck?
e: A traditional 401(k) lets employees contribute pre-tax money directly from each paycheck, which lowers taxable income now; withdrawals in retirement are taxed. A Roth IRA uses after-tax money, and a taxable brokerage account has no tax advantage.

q: An investor holds a stock for more than one year before selling it at a profit. The gain is taxed as a
o: long-term capital gain, usually at a lower rate
short-term capital gain at ordinary income rates
e: Profits on investments held more than one year are long-term capital gains, taxed at 0%, 15% or 20% depending on income. That's usually lower than the ordinary income rates (up to 37%) applied to short-term gains on investments held a year or less.

q: Banks must report cash transactions over $10,000 to the government to help prevent
e: Under the Bank Secrecy Act, banks file a Currency Transaction Report for cash transactions over $10,000 and Suspicious Activity Reports for unusual activity. These reports help authorities trace and stop money laundering, where criminals try to make illegal money look legitimate.

q: A bank checks a new customer's identity documents before opening an account. This is required by
e: Know-your-customer (KYC) and anti-money-laundering rules, including the customer identification program required after the USA PATRIOT Act, make banks verify who customers are before opening accounts. That helps stop fraud, money laundering and terrorist financing.

q: Which form of business ownership protects the owners' personal assets from business debts while letting profits pass through to their personal tax returns?
e: A limited liability company (LLC) protects owners' personal assets from business debts and lawsuits, while profits pass through to owners' personal tax returns, avoiding corporate double taxation. Sole proprietors and general partners have unlimited personal liability.

q: An S corporation differs from a C corporation mainly because an S corporation
o: passes profits through to owners' personal tax returns, avoiding double taxation
e: An S corporation passes profits and losses through to shareholders' personal tax returns, so the business itself doesn't pay corporate income tax, avoiding double taxation. In exchange it's limited to 100 shareholders, generally U.S. citizens or residents, and one class of stock.

q: For a contract to be legally binding, which element is required?
o: Offer and acceptance between parties who have legal capacity
A written document in every case
e: A binding contract needs an offer and acceptance (agreement), consideration, parties with legal capacity (generally adults of sound mind) and a legal purpose. Many contracts can be oral, and no notary or minimum dollar amount is generally required.

q: A fraudster joins a church community, earns members' trust, then sells them a fake 'guaranteed' investment. This is an example of
e: Affinity fraud targets members of an identifiable group, such as a religious, ethnic, cultural or professional community. The fraudster exploits the trust members have in someone who seems to be 'one of us,' so victims skip their normal due diligence. Front-running and churning are broker abuses.

q: A bank requires that the employee who opens new vendor accounts can't also approve payments to vendors. This compliance control is called
